PullRequest.Title: chore: use Node.js 24 in Copilot and sanity CI pipelines
PullRequest.Body:
This PR mirrors #346216 to get it merged into main.
All credit goes to @swarnava.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added boundary call, its placement before cache restoration, and the 28-job template fan-out are explicit in repository YAML. Exact nodejs.org latency and stall prevalence are uncertain, which limits severity, but the mechanism and critical-path regression are direct.
Findings.PerformanceResource: HTTPS requests to nodejs.org and blocked CI agents
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The unconditional lookup runs once for every sanity job; the standalone and release sanity stages expand the template to as many as 28 parallel OS/architecture jobs, so one pipeline produces up to 28 concurrent version-resolution requests even with fully warm Node and node_modules caches.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased sanity-pipeline latency and an avoidable burst of outbound network I/O; any slow lookup blocks that job before cache restoration and can delay stage completion by the configured request timeout.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: SANITY_NODE_VERSION was pinned to 22.22.0, so a warm job proceeded directly to the Azure pipeline caches and install-node exited from the restored Node cache without contacting nodejs.org.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each non-Windows job now unconditionally downloads latest-v24.x/SHASUMS256.txt before restoring either cache; the analogous added PowerShell branch does the same for Windows. This happens independently in every expanded job.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 182 executes curl against nodejs.org unconditionally in the per-job sanity template, before the Node cache at line 192; the diff replaced the prior fixed SANITY_NODE_VERSION with a version spec that requires this lookup.
Findings.Title: Resolve the Node release once per sanity pipeline
Findings.Impact: Every sanity run adds up to 28 concurrent nodejs.org calls. Under the already-documented endpoint stalls, an otherwise warm job can spend up to the bounded lookup time doing no useful work, and the slowest affected job extends the sanity stage.
Findings.Evidence: product-sanity-tests.yml instantiates this template 28 times in one stage, and product-build-template.yml instantiates the same platform matrix for published builds. The lookup is on each job's critical path before Cache@2. The existing comment immediately below notes that nodejs.org sometimes stalls from the shared agent pools, while this request permits up to 60 seconds and retries. Cache hits cannot eliminate the new request.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve the exact 24.x version once in a small preparation job and pass it as an output to all sanity jobs, or pin the exact version centrally and update it deliberately; retain the resolved version in both cache keys so new releases still receive fresh caches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Standalone and published-build sanity-test matrix startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each platform job checks out the sparse test tree, performs the newly added Node release lookup, restores the Node and node_modules caches, installs Node/dependencies on misses, compiles, and runs sanity tests. The new lookup must finish before either cache can be consulted; none of this work is off the individual job's critical path, and the stage waits for all matrix jobs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download latest-v24.x/SHASUMS256.txt to resolve the exact Node release
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per expanded job, up to 28 per pipeline run, concurrently; retries remain local to each job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The exact 22.22.0 version was already known, so warm jobs made zero nodejs.org requests before cache restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks each job before any cache restore; the slowest affected job can extend stage completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore Node and node_modules through Azure Cache@2
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two cache operations per platform job; 56 at the 28-job maximum.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both caches existed; the Node cache was keyed by the fixed version, while node_modules was reusable across Node patches because its key omitted Node.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both restores are on the setup critical path. The Node version newly participates in the node_modules key, causing one cold matrix after each resolved patch change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download Node checksum and archive from nodejs.org on a Node-cache miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on warm caches; on cold caches, one checksum plus one archive per job per attempt, with up to four attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fallback existed for 22.22.0 and was bypassed on a cache hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks dependency setup only on cache misses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install pnpm packages from the configured registry when node_modules is not restored
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero project installs on a warm node_modules cache; one pnpm install per cold job, up to 28 following a Node patch change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The install already existed, but adding Node to its cache key makes a newly resolved patch deliberately trigger a cold install.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks compile and tests on misses.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The standalone pipeline has 28 OS/architecture jobs, and a full published-build sanity stage has the same effective maximum of 28. There is no grouping or coalescing of release lookup across jobs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The jobs are independent members of one stage and may execute concurrently subject to agent-pool capacity. Consequently the changed lookup can burst to 28 concurrent nodejs.org requests; there is no shared limiter or preparation job.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm Node and node_modules caches avoid archive download and pnpm install, but cannot avoid the newly unconditional release lookup because it precedes Cache@2. On a new Node patch, the versioned Node and node_modules keys intentionally make all platform caches cold; failed release lookups are not negatively cached or coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the unconditional curl, its pre-cache ordering, and the 28-job expansion are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal response time for the small checksum file and frequency of endpoint stalls are not measured. The template nevertheless documents nodejs.org stalls on these shared pools and bounds this new request at 60 seconds with retries, so the latency mechanism is certain while exact minutes lost per run vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: the diff changes a warm-cache path from no nodejs.org request to one request in every matrix job, producing avoidable critical-path network work and a concurrent burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot extension product and recovery build/test setup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After checkout, setup-steps runs NodeTool, registry setup, a Node-version-aware node_modules cache-key computation, Cache@2, and dependency installation before build/test/package work. NodeTool remains on the critical path. Recovery invokes the shared setup in buildSteps and testSteps; the regular product job invokes it once.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/install Node 24.x through NodeTool with checkLatest enabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One task execution per setup invocation: one in the regular product job and setup in recovery build/test contexts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: NodeTool requested pinned 22.21.x without checkLatest; whether the external task performed a network request on a warm agent is not repository-visible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before cache-key generation and all build/test work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore node_modules cache and install dependencies on miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache lookup per setup invocation; one dependency install on each miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The cache existed, but its computed key did not receive the exact Node version argument.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks build and tests; a Node patch now intentionally selects a fresh cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout vscode-capi/localization repositories and access package registries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing fixed checkouts and package operations per job, not scaled by changed input collections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same checkouts and package operations under Node 22.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing setup/build boundaries remain critical, but the diff does not increase their call count except through possible cache invalidation when Node changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One setup invocation in the regular Copilot product job and up to two separate recovery template jobs/contexts. The cache key computation itself is constant-size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most the external recovery template's build and test jobs may overlap; no repository-visible loop fans this setup across a large collection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The node_modules key now includes process.versions.node, correctly separating dependencies when the latest 24.x patch changes. Warm-cache behavior for NodeTool with checkLatest is implemented by an external Azure task and cannot be established from this repository; dependency cache hits still avoid npm/pnpm installation according to the existing template flow.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Medium for a latest-version check being requested; low for proving an additional network call on every warm invocation from repository evidence alone.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: NodeTool's exact remote-check protocol, agent tool-cache state, and recovery template job topology are external to this repository. Therefore the added checkLatest flag alone is insufficient to quantify a concrete recurring delay.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the version-aware dependency key is bounded and appropriate, while the external NodeTool behavior does not provide enough in-repository evidence for a high-confidence performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot chat-lib package build and three-platform test matrix
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The package build provisions Node, configures npm/pnpm, installs/extracts/builds chat-lib, then the external packaging template runs tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows with the selected Node version. Provisioning and package installs are on each job's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/install Node for the package build through NodeTool with checkLatest
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One build-side task per package pipeline invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The task requested Node 22.x without checkLatest.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provision Node for Linux, macOS, and Windows test jobs through the external npm-package template
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three platform/version combinations, unchanged in count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three jobs provisioned Node 22.x rather than 24.x.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tool provisioning precedes tests; download occurs only if the external template/task cannot satisfy the version from its cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install workspace/chat-lib dependencies from the configured package registry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing fixed install steps per build/test job; no changed loop cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same install operations ran under Node 22.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One package build plus three test platforms. The changed version list does not add platforms or test repetitions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three platform tests may run concurrently under the external template; no changed shared limiter or per-item expansion is visible.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Changing from Node 22.x to 24.x can cause the expected one-time tool/dependency cold caches. The build-side NodeTool now requests checkLatest, but its warm-cache lookup behavior is external. Existing pnpm installs and registry configuration are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that job/platform cardinality is unchanged; medium that checkLatest causes extra warm-path work because implementation is external.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External template caching and NodeTool implementation are not present, so one-time migration misses can be identified but recurring network cost from checkLatest cannot be proven or timed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this is a bounded runtime-version migration with unchanged test fan-out, and repository evidence does not establish a recurring actionable regression beyond the separately reported sanity fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed CI YAML files and their relevant callers/templates. One medium-confidence-in-magnitude, high-confidence-in-mechanism regression was submitted: unconditional latest-version resolution fans out across up to 28 sanity jobs before caches. Other changes either preserve bounded cardinality, intentionally invalidate caches on Node changes, or depend on external task behavior that cannot support another high-confidence finding.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
